newsitem.title: GERMANY: German metal union says wins new pay breakthrough.
newsitem.headline: German metal union says wins new pay breakthrough.

text.p: German metal and engineering trade union IG Metall said on Sunday negotiators in the state of Baden-Wuerttemberg had agreed a wage deal which maintained full sick pay for some 300,000 employees there.

An IG Metall spokesman said in response to enquiries that a deal had been reached on Thursday night which mirrored a breakthrough deal reached earlier the same day in the smaller state of Lower Saxony.

The news came as representatives of the Gesamtmetall employers' federation met in Frankfurt to discuss the deal reached in Lower Saxony, with Gesamtmetall officials saying before the meeting that the deal was likely to be sharply criticised.
According to the IG Metall spokesman, the new deal was similar to the Lower Saxony deal "in all main points".
Aside from the maintenance of full sick pay, wages for workers in the southern part of the Baden-Wuerttemberg will rise by 1.5 percent next year and an additional 2.5 percent in 1998.
The deal does not apply to workers in the northern part of Baden-Wuerttemberg.
Gesamtmetall, meeting to rethink its negotiating strategy after a big setback in its bid to push through sick pay cuts and reduce labour costs, had no immediate comment.
